Thanks Hannah — helpful summary. A couple quick clarifications from our side before NetOps digs into the matrix: 

- We generally prefer PrivateLink for partner integrations where possible, but we've hit throughput limits in the past with high-traffic inference; can you include expected per-connection throughput estimates (tokens/sec) or recommended concurrency targets for the pilot?
- On TLS interception: Security has a policy of MITM only for outbound to external SaaS — they'll review whether Redwood's service certs can be accepted by our proxy. For now please assume we will have a TLS-terminating proxy in front of the outbound flow.
- For allowlist: we need explicit port ranges per service. Can you confirm ports needed for model inference, manifests, and health checks separately?

David (NetOps) — can you review the attached matrix and tell us if any of these CIDRs conflict with existing B2B peering? If PrivateLink looks better, we may need a procurement ticket for cross-account privatelink setup.

Appended technical detail below — pulled from our Private deployment playbook. I've also attached a cleaned-up network matrix with port columns per your ask.

> Ayesha — throughput and port breakout:

- Throughput guidance (pilot): a single RDW inference endpoint (1 GPU-backed model instance) typically sustains ~150–200 tokens/sec with a 2k token context for T4-class instances. For large production workloads we recommend Dedicated pools or multiple endpoints behind a load balancer; we can run a quick concurrency/baseline test during the pilot window.

- Ports (egress/outbound from your VPC to Redwood control plane and inference endpoints):
  - 443 (HTTPS) — primary for inference and control plane (TLS).
  - 5222 (optional) — health/keepalive telemetry if you enable our low-latency telemetry channel.
  - 80 (optional) — only for health probe fallbacks (we recommend restricting).
  - 9000–9100 (internal) — only used for internal debug sessions; do not open unless expressly requested.

- PrivateLink vs peering tradeoffs (brief):
  - PrivateLink: simpler cross-account model, IPs owned by AWS, good for strict egress allowlist patterns; requires per-region endpoint setup and may need a procurement request for interface endpoints.
  - VPC peering: lower latency for heavy throughput but requires routing/overlap checks and potential NAT/eBPF config on your side; also adds cross-account routing complexity.

Attachments: updated matrix (clearview_network_matrix_v2.xlsx) and a 1-page pilot checklist.

Next suggested action: David/NetOps to confirm whether PrivateLink procurement is acceptable; if yes, Marissa and I will schedule a 1-hour pilot window (we'll provide a controlled IP set and a link to a smoke workload).

-Karthik

Hi all — thanks for the notes. Short scheduling note and proposed pilot runbook: 

Pilot runbook (60–90 minutes):
- Preflight: ClearView to open the allowlist for the 3 IPs in the v2 matrix and confirm TLS proxy behavior for the pilot window (we can work with a short CA chain if needed).
- Test: Redwood will route a smoke workload (100 concurrent requests, short prompts) against a sandboxed PrivateLink/peered endpoint.
- Observe: We capture request latency, tokens/sec, and a binary pass/fail on metric regressions (alerts if 95th percentile latency > 600ms).
- Post: brief 30-minute readout with NetOps + Security.

Please confirm availability next Tue or Wed morning PST for the pilot (we have slots 9:30–11:00 PST both days). If David prefers a NetOps-only staging kickoff, I'm happy to spin that up.
